stories.headline: Iran names Mojtaba Khamenei as new supreme leader, signaling hardliner continuity amid war

key_facts.fact: Iran's 88-member Assembly of Experts named Mojtaba Khamenei, 56, as the new supreme leader on Sunday March 8, succeeding his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei who was killed in the first wave of US-Israeli strikes on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Mojtaba Khamenei will replace his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as Iran's new supreme leader. A statement by the Assembly of Experts - an 88-member clerical body tasked with selecting the supreme leader - was read aloud by a presenter on state TV.

key_facts.fact: This is the first time since the 1979 Islamic Revolution that Iran's supreme leadership has passed from father to son, marking a dynastic transfer unprecedented in the Republic's history.
key_facts.excerpt: Mojtaba Khamenei's elevation marks the first time since the 1979 Islamic revolution that Iran's supreme leadership has passed from father to son.

key_facts.fact: Key political leaders, the IRGC, and the armed forces quickly pledged allegiance to Mojtaba. Iran's President Pezeshkian called the appointment a 'new era of dignity and strength' for the nation.
key_facts.excerpt: Key political leaders, the powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the armed forces were quick to pledge their backing to the new leader. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said the appointment heralded a 'new era of dignity and strength' for the nation.

key_facts.fact: US President Trump had previously said appointing Khamenei's son would be an unacceptable choice, insisting the US should have a say in selecting the new leader.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump insisted on US having say in selection of new leader

key_facts.fact: Mojtaba is known for his close ties with the IRGC and vast business networks built under his father, and is widely expected to continue hardline policies.
key_facts.excerpt: Mojtaba is often described as enigmatic and, at the same time, one of the most influential figures in Iran's power corridors. He is known to have kept close links with the powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which many believe calls the shots in the country.

stories.headline: Oil briefly hits $120/barrel as Iran war intensifies, Nikkei plunges 7% and Dow futures drop 1,000 points

key_facts.fact: Brent crude surged to as high as $119.50 per barrel early Monday, later trading above $101, up 9%. West Texas Intermediate reached $120 per barrel in overnight trading before paring gains.
key_facts.excerpt: The price for a barrel of Brent crude, the international standard, surged to as high $119.50 per barrel early in the day but later was trading above $101 per barrel, up 9%.

key_facts.fact: Japan's Nikkei 225 plummeted 7% to 51,740.46, its lowest level since January 9. The broader Topix fell 5.6%. Nikkei futures fell as much as 7.8%, close to triggering a circuit breaker.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's Nikkei average fell 7% to a two-month low on Monday amid a broad selloff, as a surge in oil prices fanned fears of inflation and an economic slowdown. The Nikkei fell 6.98% to 51,740.46, its lowest level since January 9.

key_facts.fact: Dow Jones futures crashed 1,011 points (-2.13%), S&P 500 futures dropped 2.01%, and Nasdaq futures fell 2.31% Sunday night. By Monday's close the S&P 500 fell 0.5% after dropping as much as 1.5% in the morning.
key_facts.excerpt: Dow Jones futures crashed 1,011 points (-2.13%). S&P 500 futures down 2.01%. Nasdaq futures lost 2.31%.

key_facts.fact: The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed, preventing Persian Gulf oil producers from exporting crude. Iraq's oil output has collapsed 60% as storage capacity filled.
key_facts.excerpt: The waterway 'remains effectively closed,' preventing Persian Gulf oil producers from exporting crude. Iraq's output has collapsed 60% as storage capacity filled.

key_facts.fact: Oil prices have skyrocketed 66% since the Iran war began on February 28, with an 80% probability of gas prices reaching $4 per gallon within a month.

stories.headline: IRGC launches waves 27-30 of Operation True Promise 4 with new solid-fuel missiles

key_facts.fact: The IRGC launched waves 27 through 30 of Operation True Promise 4 over March 8-9, including coordinated drone and missile strikes against American and Israeli targets using newly developed solid-fuel missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) has announced carrying out the 27th wave of Operation True Promise 4... the strikes included missile counteroffensives against Israeli military objectives... using newly developed solid-fuel missiles.

key_facts.fact: The 29th wave struck targets in Tel Aviv, the Negev Desert, and a US air base in the region using 'a new generation of missiles operated by the Aerospace Force of the IRGC.'
key_facts.excerpt: The strikes were directed at targets in Tel Aviv, the Negev Desert, and a U.S. air base in the region, under the slogan 'Ali bin Abi Taleb.' According to Iranian officials...

key_facts.fact: The 27th wave included a joint IRGC operation targeting a US helicopter base at Al-Ada'iri, Kuwait. Lebanese Hezbollah and the Islamic Resistance in Iraq joined the operations, widening the regional scope.
key_facts.excerpt: Central to the Sunday strikes was a joint operation by the IRGC, which targeted a US helicopter base in Al-Ada'iri, Kuwait... The regional scope of the conflict has widened as the Lebanese Hezbollah movement and the Islamic Resistance in Iraq joined the front.

key_facts.fact: Iran's foreign ministry stated its self-defence operations will continue until US-Israel attacks end or the UN acts, citing Article 51 of the UN Charter.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran said on Sunday that it will continue... Iran cites UN Charter Article 51 to justify military response.

key_facts.fact: The IRGC claimed it could sustain an 'intense war' for six months, signaling readiness for a protracted conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran Guards say can fight 'intense war' for six months

stories.headline: Desalination plants hit in Bahrain and Iran as water infrastructure becomes new front in the war

key_facts.fact: An Iranian drone attack damaged a water desalination plant in Bahrain, the first targeting of such a facility in a Gulf nation during the war. Three people were injured.
key_facts.excerpt: Bahrain says the latest Iranian attacks on the country have damaged a water desalination plant and injured three people as Tehran continues its air campaign against its Gulf neighbours.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi said a US airstrike damaged a freshwater desalination plant on Qeshm Island, cutting water supply to 30 villages, and warned: 'the U.S. set this precedent, not Iran.'
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. airstrike damaged Iran's desalination plant on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, affecting water access. Iran's foreign minister stated the strike 'cut into the water supply to 30 villages.'

key_facts.fact: Desalination plants supply water to millions of residents across the Gulf, creating extreme vulnerability in the parched desert nations where alternatives are limited.
key_facts.excerpt: Water... Desalination plants supply water to millions of residents in the region.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Red Crescent reported about 10,000 civilian structures across the country had been damaged, including homes, schools, and medical facilities. At least 1,230 people have been killed in Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Red Crescent Society reported 'about 10,000 civilian structures across the country had been damaged,' including homes, schools, and medical facilities.

stories.headline: US and Israel discuss special forces mission to seize Iran's 450 kg of enriched uranium

key_facts.fact: The US and Israel are discussing sending special operations forces into Iran to secure 450 kilograms of 60% enriched uranium that the White House believes could be weaponized within weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: The White House believes the regime's 450 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60% could be weaponized within weeks. Seizing the nuclear material would likely require U.S. or Israeli troops to enter Iran and penetrate heavily fortified underground facilities.

key_facts.fact: Trump told reporters on Air Force One: 'Right now we're just decimating them, but we haven't gone after it. But something we could do later on. We wouldn't do it now.'
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One, Trump suggested the possibility of a ground operation had not been ruled out, saying U.S. forces could move in at a later stage of the conflict if necessary. 'Right now we're just decimating them, but we haven't gone after it,' Trump said.

key_facts.fact: Intelligence sources warn Iran's uranium stockpile could build 11 nuclear bombs. Facilities at Isfahan, Fordow, and Natanz are among the potential targets for any covert operation.
key_facts.excerpt: Washington and Tel Aviv examine covert Special Forces operations targeting Iran's underground nuclear facilities at Isfahan, Fordow and Natanz amid intelligence fears that 450kg of highly enriched uranium could rapidly become weapons-grade.

key_facts.fact: The operation would likely take place only after both countries conclude that Iran's armed forces no longer pose a serious threat to the units involved. It remains unclear if US, Israeli, or joint forces would carry it out.
key_facts.excerpt: The operation would likely take place only after both countries conclude that Iran's armed forces no longer pose a serious threat to the units involved.

key_facts.fact: UN atomic inspectors have not verified the location of Iran's highly enriched uranium for almost nine months, increasing uncertainty about whether it has been moved.
key_facts.excerpt: Uncertainty over Tehran's highly enriched uranium has intensified because it is almost nine months since UN atomic inspectors last verified its location.

stories.headline: France announces EU-led naval escort mission to reopen Strait of Hormuz after 'hot phase' of war

key_facts.fact: French President Macron announced from Cyprus on Monday that France and allies are preparing a 'purely defensive' escort mission for container ships and tankers through the Strait of Hormuz once the most intense phase of the war ends.
key_facts.excerpt: French President Emmanuel Macron has said France and its allies are preparing a 'purely defensive' mission to escort vessels through the Strait of Hormuz once the 'most intense phase' of the US-Israeli war on Iran ends.

key_facts.fact: France will send two frigates as part of the EU's Aspides naval mission in the Red Sea, and the Hormuz mission would comprise both European and non-European navies.
key_facts.excerpt: France will send two frigates as part of the European Union's naval mission Aspides in the Red Sea. 'We are in the process of setting up a purely defensive, purely escort mission, which must be prepared together with both European and non-European states.'

key_facts.fact: The Strait of Hormuz carries roughly one-fifth of the world's crude oil and maritime traffic there has nearly halted since the war began on February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow waterway in the Persian Gulf through which roughly one-fifth of the world's crude oil passes. Maritime traffic there has nearly halted since the war began.

key_facts.fact: Iran fired a second missile at Turkey on Monday, which was shot down by NATO air defenses, risking drawing NATO assets into Iran's confrontation with the West.
key_facts.excerpt: It also fired a second missile at Turkey on Monday, which was shot down by Nato air-defences, risking drawing Nato assets in the region into Iran's confrontation.

key_facts.fact: Macron discussed the mission with Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis and Cypriot President Christodoulides at a military base in Paphos, Cyprus.
key_facts.excerpt: Emmanuel Macron told reporters at a military base in Cyprus that he discussed the potential mission with his Greek and Cypriot counterparts, Kyriakos Mitsotakis and Nikos Christodoulides.

stories.headline: Russia sits back on Iran war, betting on higher oil revenues and depleted Western arsenals

key_facts.fact: Russia is profiting from a surge in energy prices caused by the Iran war's disruption to tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and damage to Gulf energy facilities, expecting the windfall to fund its Ukraine operations and plug its budget deficit.
key_facts.excerpt: Moscow is profiting from a spike in oil prices, and the Kremlin bets a windfall from prolonged hostilities could help boost its coffers to pay for military operations in Ukraine and plug a budget deficit.

key_facts.fact: India, China, and Turkey are expected to increase purchases of Russian crude as Middle East supply disruptions drive buyers toward alternative suppliers.
key_facts.excerpt: India, China, and Turkey could increase purchases of Russian crude.

key_facts.fact: Moscow expects the Iran war to divert Western attention from Ukraine and deplete Western military arsenals, weakening support for Kyiv.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia also hopes the war pulls attention away from Ukraine and depletes Western arsenals.

key_facts.fact: Analysts say a weakened Iran would not dramatically dent Putin's authority. Iran has always been 'something of a strategic frenemy' to Russia, and the war could make Tehran a 'more amenable partner.'
key_facts.excerpt: A weakened Iran wouldn't dramatically dent Vladimir Putin's authority at home or abroad, analysts said. Iran has always been 'something of a strategic frenemy' to Russia, one expert said, and the war could make Tehran a more amenable partner.

key_facts.fact: Putin sent condolences to Pezeshkian condemning Khamenei's killing as a 'cynical violation of all norms of human morality and international law' but took no visible action to support Iran militarily.
key_facts.excerpt: Putin sent his condolences to Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, condemning the killing of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as a 'cynical violation of all norms of human morality and international law.'

stories.headline: Seventh US service member dies from injuries sustained in Iranian attack on Saudi Arabia

key_facts.fact: A US Army soldier died Saturday from injuries received during Iran's initial wave of attacks on March 1 in Saudi Arabia, bringing the total number of American troops killed in the Iran war to seven.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military announced an American service member has died of injuries sustained during an Iranian attack on troops stationed in Saudi Arabia. The seventh American service member killed in the Iran war was an Army soldier.

key_facts.fact: The first six killed were Army reservists who died in a March 1 drone strike on a command center at a Kuwaiti port: Maj. Jeffrey O'Brien, Capt. Cody Khork, CW3 Robert Marzan, SFC Nicole Amor, SFC Noah Tietjens, and Sgt. Declan Coady.

Declan Coady, 20, of West Des Moines, Iowa, who were killed in a drone strike at a command center in Kuwait.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command announced the death on X, stating the service member was 'seriously wounded at the scene of an attack on U.S. troops in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.'
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon announced the death of a U.S. Army soldier who was injured during a March 1 Iranian attack on U.S. troops in Saudi Arabia.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia warned Tehran that continued attacks on the kingdom and its energy sector could push Riyadh to respond in kind, according to four sources familiar with the matter cited by Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia has told Tehran that while it favours a diplomatic settlement to Iran's conflict with the United States, continued attacks on the kingdom and its energy sector could push Riyadh to respond in kind, four sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

key_facts.fact: The warning was delivered during a call between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iranian counterpart Abbas Araqchi, days before Pezeshkian's public apology to Gulf states.
key_facts.excerpt: The warning was delivered during a call two days earlier between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araqchi.

stories.headline: Roche's Gazyva shows breakthrough lupus results in Phase III trial published in NEJM

key_facts.fact: Roche's Phase III ALLEGORY trial showed 76.7% of lupus patients on Gazyva (obinutuzumab) plus standard therapy achieved SRI-4 improvement at week 52, versus 53.5% on placebo — a 23.1 percentage point difference (p<0.001).
key_facts.excerpt: Over three quarters (76.7%) of people treated with Gazyva plus standard therapy achieved at least a four-point improvement in SRI-4 at week 52, versus 53.5% on placebo.

key_facts.fact: Remission rates (DORIS criteria) at week 52 were 35.1% for Gazyva vs 13.8% for placebo — more than doubling the remission rate. The study enrolled approximately 300 patients in a 1:1 randomization.
key_facts.excerpt: Remission Rate (DORIS) at Week 52: Gazyva: 35.1% | Placebo: 13.8%. Total enrolled: Approximately 300 patients. Randomization: 1:1 ratio.

key_facts.fact: If approved, Gazyva would be the first Type II anti-CD20 therapy for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), which affects more than 3 million people worldwide.
key_facts.excerpt: If approved, Gazyva/Gazyvaro would be the first Type II anti-CD20 therapy for SLE to directly target B cells, a key driver of inflammation and disease activity. SLE is a potentially life-threatening autoimmune disease that affects more than three million people worldwide.

key_facts.fact: The detailed results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine and presented at the European Lupus Meeting (SLEuro 2026).
key_facts.excerpt: A detailed analysis of the phase III ALLEGORY trial of Gazyva/Gazyvaro (obinutuzumab) in adults with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) was published in the New England Journal of Medicine.

stories.headline: FDA plans to ease biosimilar testing rules, potentially cutting $20M per drug from development costs

key_facts.fact: The FDA plans to issue draft guidance as soon as Monday March 10 that would reduce the need for certain studies used to demonstrate biosimilar medicines match their brand-name counterparts.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA is expected to issue draft guidance as soon as Monday that would reduce the need for certain studies used to show that biosimilar medicines match the brand-name treatments they are based on.

key_facts.fact: The change could cut about $20 million from the cost of developing a biosimilar drug, according to Bloomberg, as part of a broader FDA effort to increase competition and lower medicine prices.
key_facts.excerpt: The change could cut about $20 million from the cost of developing a biosimilar, according to Bloomberg. The policy is part of a broader FDA effort to make it easier for companies to win approval for such drugs.

key_facts.fact: The policy is part of FDA Commissioner Marty Makary's broader agenda of 'radical transparency' and streamlining drug approvals, though the agency has faced criticism for reducing advisory committee meetings by 72% in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The agency held 14 advisory committee meetings in 2025, down from 38 in 2024 and 29 in 2023. The number of advisory committee meetings related to drugs decreased by 72% last year.
